title: Matching objects of a simplicial object in a category with finite limits
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits] and a final object $e$, and let $K$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal C$ with face maps $d_i$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. For $n\geq2$ let $D_n(K)$ be the finite diagram in $\mathcal C$ with objects $K^{(i)}_{n-1}=K_{n-1}$ ($0\leq i\leq n$) and $K^{(i,j)}_{n-2}=K_{n-2}$ ($0\leq i<j\leq n$) and arrows $d_{j-1}:K^{(i)}_{n-1}\to K^{(i,j)}_{n-2}$ and $d_i:K^{(j)}_{n-1}\to K^{(i,j)}_{n-2}$ for $0\leq i<j\leq n$; let $D_1(K)$ be the diagram with the two objects $K^{(0)}_0=K^{(1)}_0=K_0$ and no arrows; let $D_0(K)$ be the empty diagram. Then: (1) for every $n\geq0$ the diagram $D_n(K)$ has a limit $M_n(K)$ in $\mathcal C$ (for $n=0$ this is a final object, for $n=1$ a product $K_0\times K_0$), unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with the limit projections; for $n\geq1$ write $\mathrm{pr}_i:M_n(K)\to K_{n-1}$ for the projection to $K^{(i)}_{n-1}$, $0\leq i\leq n$. (2) For $n\geq1$ and every object $W$ of $\mathcal C$, the map $g\mapsto(\mathrm{pr}_0\circ g,\dots,\mathrm{pr}_n\circ g)$ is a bijection, natural in $W$, from the morphisms $W\to M_n(K)$ onto the tuples $(x_0,\dots,x_n)$ of morphisms $x_i:W\to K_{n-1}$ satisfying $d_{j-1}\circ x_i=d_i\circ x_j$ for all $0\leq i<j\leq n$ (no condition when $n=1$). (3) For $n\geq2$ the face maps $d_i:K_n\to K_{n-1}$ satisfy $d_{j-1}\circ d_i=d_i\circ d_j:K_n\to K_{n-2}$ for all $0\leq i<j\leq n$; hence for every $n\geq1$ there is a unique morphism $\mu_n:K_n\to M_n(K)$, the *matching morphism*, with $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\mu_n=d_i$ for $0\leq i\leq n$; and $\mu_0:K_0\to M_0(K)$ denotes the unique morphism to the final object.

proof.text: For each n, D_n(K) is a finite diagram: for n=0 it is empty, for n=1 it has two objects and no arrows, and for n≥2 it has finitely many indexed objects and arrows because the index sets 0≤i≤n and 0≤i<j≤n are finite. Since C has finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits], D_n(K) has a limit M_n(K). The empty limit is a final object and the two-object limit for n=1 is a product; the universal property gives uniqueness up to unique isomorphism preserving the projections.

source.place: Categories, Section 4.18, tag 04AS, together with Lemma 002O (lemma-finite-limits-exist); simplicial.tex Lemma 0186 (lemma-formula-limit), construction of the finite boundary diagram

proof.text: For n≥1, the universal property of the limit M_n(K) identifies a morphism g:W→M_n(K) with its projections x_i=pr_i∘g. Each cone gives a tuple satisfying d_{j-1}∘x_i=d_i∘x_j, because the two arrows from K_{n-1}^{(i)} and K_{n-1}^{(j)} to K_{n-2}^{(i,j)} are part of D_n(K). Conversely, a tuple satisfying these equations is a cone on D_n(K): for n=1 there are no compatibility equations, and for n≥2 the component at K_{n-2}^{(i,j)} is the common composite d_{j-1}∘x_i=d_i∘x_j; the limit property gives a unique g. Precomposition with a morphism W'→W commutes with all projections, so the bijection is natural in W.

proof.text: For n≥2, the simplicial face identity δ^{n}_j∘δ^{n-1}_i=δ^{n}_i∘δ^{n-1}_{j-1} for 0≤i<j≤n [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-face-identity] (applied with n-1≥1), transported by the contravariant functor K with d_i=K(δ_i) [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], gives d_{j-1}∘d_i=d_i∘d_j:K_n→K_{n-2} for every i<j, so the tuple (d_0,…,d_n) of maps K_n→K_{n-1} satisfies the compatibility equations of step 2. Hence there is a unique morphism μ_n:K_n→M_n(K) with pr_i∘μ_n=d_i. For n=1 the same conclusion follows from the absence of compatibility equations, and for n=0 the unique map K_0→M_0(K) exists because M_0(K) is final. This is the matching morphism in every degree.

lean.statement: theorem matching_object_succ_succ {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteLimits C] (K : SimplicialObject C) (n : ℕ) : ∃ c : Cone (matchingBoundaryIndex K n).multicospan, Nonempty (IsLimit c) ∧ (∀ (c' : Cone (matchingBoundaryIndex K n).multicospan), Nonempty (IsLimit c') → ∃! α : c.pt ≅ c'.pt, ∀ j, α.hom ≫ c'.π.app j = c.π.app j) ∧ (∃ E : ∀ W : C, (W ⟶ c.pt) ≃ {x : Fin (n + 3) → (W ⟶ K _⦋n + 1⦌) // ∀ p : (matchingBoundaryShape n).R, x p.val.1 ≫ (matchingBoundaryIndex K n).fst p = x p.val.2 ≫ (matchingBoundaryIndex K n).snd p}, (∀ (W : C) (g : W ⟶ c.pt) (i : Fin (n + 3)), (E W g).val i = g ≫ c.π.app (WalkingMulticospan.left i)) ∧ (∀ (W W' : C) (f : W' ⟶ W) (g : W ⟶ c.pt) (i : Fin (n + 3)), (E W' (f ≫ g)).val i = f ≫ (E W g).val i)) ∧ (∀ p : (matchingBoundaryShape n).R, K.δ p.val.1 ≫ (matchingBoundaryIndex K n).fst p = K.δ p.val.2 ≫ (matchingBoundaryIndex K n).snd p) ∧ (∃! μ : K _⦋n + 2⦌ ⟶ c.pt, ∀ i : Fin (n + 3), μ ≫ c.π.app (WalkingMulticospan.left i) = K.δ i)
